description: High-quality answer criteria for the Performance Review - Focused Improvement Getting Started interview. Employee self-evaluation in preparation for a review focused on specific performance concerns and needed improvement.

terms.label: Role Expectations & Performance Standards
terms.description: Responsibilities, expectations, or performance standards most important to clarify for the role right now.

terms.label: Specific Performance Concerns
terms.description: The specific performance concerns identified as needing improvement and how the employee understands them.

terms.label: Evidence, Examples & Impact
terms.description: Examples, feedback, outcomes, and evidence explaining the concerns and their impact.

terms.label: Causes, Context & Contributing Factors
terms.description: Factors contributing to the performance concerns and their locus of control.

terms.label: Actions Already Taken
terms.description: Steps already taken to address the concerns and what changed as a result.

terms.label: Support, Resources & Clarification Needed
terms.description: Support, resources, clarification, coaching, or changes that would help meet expectations.

terms.label: Improvement Plan & Timeline
terms.description: Specific improvements to make next and a realistic timeline for showing progress.

terms.label: Commitment, Risks & Follow-Up
terms.description: Commitments, risks that could interfere with improvement, and how progress should be reviewed.

responseProfile.stance: Performance consistently falls materially short of expectations.
Performance has meaningful gaps and requires focused improvement.
Performance reliably fulfills the expectations of the role.
Performance significantly and consistently surpasses expectations.

primaryQuestions.question: What responsibilities, expectations, or performance standards are most important to clarify for your role right now?
answerGuidance: Your current role/title or functional position
The responsibilities, expectations, or performance standards that need the most clarification
Which responsibilities are core to your role versus temporary, expanded, or informal work
Where role scope, ownership, decision rights, or success standards feel unclear or disputed
How lack of clarity affects performance or improvement planning
Any expectations that have changed, intensified, or become more important recently

highQualityCriteria.requirement: States current role/title or functional position
highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review Focused Improvement

highQualityCriteria.requirement: Lists one or more responsibilities, expectations, or performance standards that need clarification right now
highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review Focused Improvement

highQualityCriteria.requirement: Describes each responsibility, expectation, or performance standard in concrete, understandable terms
highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review Focused Improvement

highQualityCriteria.requirement: Explains why each responsibility, expectation, or performance standard matters to current performance improvement
highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review Focused Improvement

highQualityCriteria.requirement: Distinguishes responsibilities that are core to the role from temporary assignments, expanded scope, or informal requests
highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review Focused Improvement

highQualityCriteria.requirement: Identifies any areas where role scope, ownership, decision rights, or success standards are unclear or disputed
highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review Focused Improvement

highQualityCriteria.requirement: Explains how unclear role scope, ownership, decision rights, or success standards affect performance or improvement planning
highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review Focused Improvement

highQualityCriteria.requirement: Notes any expectations that have changed, intensified, or become more important recently
highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review Focused Improvement

primaryQuestions.question: What specific areas of your performance have been identified as needing improvement, and how do you understand those concerns?
answerGuidance: The specific performance concerns, gaps, behaviors, deliverables, or outcomes that have been identified
How you understand each concern and why it is being raised
How each concern connects to role responsibilities, expectations, standards, goals, or business needs
Which concerns you agree with, do not fully understand, or see differently
Whether each concern involves results, execution, quality, communication, judgment, growth, or something else
Any concerns that need clearer examples, evidence, standards, or expectations

highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review Focused Improvement

highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review Focused Improvement

primaryQuestions.question: What examples, feedback, outcomes, or evidence help explain the performance concerns and their impact?
answerGuidance: Examples, feedback, outcomes, events, or evidence related to the concerns
What specifically happened, when it happened, and who or what was affected
How the examples connect to the concern being raised
The impact on work quality, timeliness, team outcomes, customer outcomes, manager confidence, or business results
Measurable evidence such as dates, deadlines, error rates, rework, feedback, or factual anchors
Which parts are observable facts versus interpretations, assumptions, opinions, or general impressions
Any missing evidence needed to understand the concern more accurately

highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review Focused Improvement

highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review Focused Improvement

highQualityCriteria.requirement: Explains how each example, feedback point, outcome, event, or evidence item relates to the performance concern
highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review Focused Improvement

highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review Focused Improvement

highQualityCriteria.requirement: Provides examples that show whether the concern is improving, unchanged, worsening, or inconsistent over time
highQualityCriteria.label: Performance Review Focused Improvement

highQualityCriteria.requirement: Identifies any missing or incomplete evidence needed to understand the concern more accurately

primaryQuestions.question: What factors do you believe are contributing to the performance concerns?
answerGuidance: Causes, context, constraints, obstacles, or contributing factors behind the performance concerns
Workload, time, staffing, tools, training, process, access, communication, feedback, role clarity, or dependency factors
How each factor affects performance or the ability to improve
Which factors are within your control versus shared, manager, team, organizational, or external control
Root causes versus symptoms, consequences, or secondary issues
Whether context, constraints, resources, or fairness considerations should affect how the concern is interpreted
Which factors should be addressed first, and why

primaryQuestions.question: What steps have you already taken to address the performance concerns, and what has changed as a result?

Why you took each action and which concern it was meant to address
Examples of responding to feedback, asking for clarification, changing work habits, improving quality, improving communication, or managing priorities differently
What improved, changed, stayed the same, or became clearer as a result
Evidence of progress, such as better results, fewer errors, faster turnaround, better feedback, completed tasks, or reduced rework
Actions that did not work as expected, and why
Where additional support, feedback, coaching, resources, or time was needed

primaryQuestions.question: What support, resources, clarification, coaching, or changes would help you meet expectations?
answerGuidance: Support, resources, clarification, coaching, feedback, training, or process changes that would help you meet expectations
How each need would improve performance or make improvement more realistic
Which needs require manager action, employee action, team action, organizational action, or system/process action
Examples such as coaching, feedback cadence, expectation clarification, tools, documentation, training, staffing, workload adjustment, or process change
Which needs are highest priority and why
Which needs are short-term versus longer-term supports
How the manager or organization could tell whether the support is helping

primaryQuestions.question: What commitments are you prepared to make, what risks could interfere with improvement, and how should progress be reviewed?
answerGuidance: The commitments you are prepared to make to improve performance

Why each commitment is realistic and meaningful
Risks, barriers, constraints, or unresolved issues that could interfere with improvement
Ways to reduce, monitor, or escalate risks that could block progress
How progress should be reviewed, including follow-up cadence, feedback approach, evidence, milestones, or success measures
What information should be shared during follow-up conversations so progress can be reviewed fairly and accurately
